title: Offer help, never pick the answer
statement: After repeated misses on a search or a used-up hint ladder, offer help through one button the student must tap to accept, and never pick the answer unasked.
example: After four missed taps on a hunt or hint ladder, help came as a single button the child had to tap to accept.
detail: A ruling for a Grade 3 reading course set that after four missed taps on any hunt or hint ladder, the lesson's guide offers help with a single button the child must tap to accept, and never marks the answer unprompted. It was first set on clue hunts and then extended to every used-up ladder before an automatic pick, so every backstop that picked the answer for the child after a number of tries now sits behind that one offer. No outcome was measured.
against: The record two-tries-then-the-answer gives the answer after two tries so that a student who never gets it right can still finish. The same course records an unresolved conflict for single-select checks: "during-reading checks get two attempts then a reveal) and the §3 no-reveal rule above give opposite instructions on the exact item" (grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-6/distilled/07-SCORING-FEEDBACK-XP.md, lines 223-224).

evidence.quote: After four missed taps on any hunt or ladder, Scout offers to help with a single button; the child must tap to accept, and Scout never marks the answer unprompted.
Every `reveal_after_tries` backstop that picked FOR the child is now gated behind the one ScoutOffer flow.
